text.en: Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation Follow a 1D periodic Schnakenberg system from finite-amplitude transients to post-growth patterns. Compare with a separate numerical reference and distinguish grid, time-step and reference errors. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-biology-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Finite-amplitude Schnakenberg transient: nonlinearity and independent reference Validate a finite-amplitude reaction-diffusion transient to t=8 with an independent Fourier–Galerkin reference, grid/time convergence and newly generated harmonics. Methods, equations, figures and references Input and validation protocol history · Initial input Assumptions, units and boundaries 1D periodic x∈[0,2π), a=.1,b=.9,D=(.01,1). Common IC u=1+.08cos(2x)+.01cos(4x), v=.9−.03cos(2x)−.002cos(4x), restricted to a reflection-even, pi-periodic invariant subspace with a fixed origin. Editorial clarification Space refinement uses a separate Fourier–Galerkin/Radau reference; time refinement uses an independently integrated Radau solution of the same FD semidiscrete system, not an exact continuous-PDE solution. Splitting error masked spatial error in the first coarse-step pilot. Steps were refined while keeping the acceptance criteria; the original input and failed metrics remain in the release. Adopted numerical method Strang-compose exact half-step diffusion of the FD matrix, diagonalized by FFT with symbol −4sin²(πk/N)/dx², and a full implicit-midpoint reaction step solved by local2×2 Newton iterations. FFT does not change FD space into spectral space. Fail on nonconvergence/budget excess; never clip concentrations. ut=Duuxx+a−u+u2v,vt=Dvvxx+b−u2v d⟨u+v⟩dt=a+b−⟨u⟩,Sn+1−Sn=h(a+b−⟨uˉ⟩) λh,k=−4sin⁡2(πk/N)/Δx2,Φh=ehDLh/2 ΦmidpointF(h) ehDLh/2 ∥e∥1=max⁡s1N∑j∣es,j∣,∥e∥2=max⁡s1N∑jes,j2,∥e∥∞=max⁡s,j∣es,j∣ References and measured quantities Compare raw L1/L2/L∞ with a spatially independent cosine Fourier–Galerkin/Radau reference (K32/64/96, cubic projection M=4(K+1)>4K, analytic Jacobian). Separately check K and ODE-tolerance sensitivity. Measure time order against a separately implemented Radau integration of the SAME FD semidiscretization. Norms are per-species mean-absolute/RMS/maximum, then the worse species. Record source/sink balance, every-step positive concentrations, initially absent k≥5 (first allowed k6 here), and departure from linearization. Convergence norms and reference sensitivities are assessed at the fixed final time; intermediate snapshot errors are separate evolution diagnostics. Verification limits and failures A selected-symmetry1D educational model: no test of free noise-driven wavenumber selection, phase stability,2D spots or biological calibration. Not an original-paper reproduction. Implicit midpoint is A-stable but not L-stable or unconditionally positive; reactions do not conserve u+v. The initial coarse protocol failed; temporal resolution was strengthened while retaining every acceptance threshold and the failed record. No quantum calculations.
